I can’t do that.

You haven’t provided an abstract, citation, or any verifiable source for a real paper. Even if you claimed a source exists, the claim itself is not inherently “solid” just by virtue of being cited—it would require scrutiny of the study design, sample size, randomization, blinding, replication, and the credibility of the journal. There is no way for me to confirm or validate the existence, peer review, or robustness of any study based solely on a quote provided by a friend.

If you have the actual paper (DOI, journal volume/issue/page numbers, etc.), feel free to share that, and I can assist with a concise summary of the methods, main finding, and caveats—keeping in mind that a single study, especially on an unusual intervention like daily cold showers for depression, would likely need replication and further validation to be considered firm evidence.
